analysis.one_liner: Reliance Industries is a diversified conglomerate spanning oil-to-chemicals refining and petrochemicals, Jio's telecom and digital services, and Reliance Retail, with a growing New Energy (solar/hydrogen) push alongside.
analysis.whats_happening: RIL reported Q2 FY27 (quarter to September 2026) results on 30 October 2026 with record revenue and EBITDA, driven by a sharp O2C (refining and petrochemicals) margin recovery and steady Jio growth, while Retail profit fell on planned investment. The stock jumped roughly 11.6% on 2 November, its sharpest single-day rally in over two years. Separately, Jio Platforms - RIL's digital arm - completed a ₹30,213 crore fresh-share IPO and listed on NSE/BSE on 28 October 2026 at a 21% premium to its issue price; this was a 100% primary issue, so RIL did not sell any of its own stake and existing RIL shareholders did not automatically receive Jio shares (only a separate, capped reservation quota to apply into).
analysis.plain_terms: Reliance makes its money from three very different businesses bundled into one stock: refining fuel and chemicals, running India's largest telecom network through Jio, and running stores plus online retail. This quarter the oil-and-chemicals business did unusually well, Jio kept growing steadily, but the retail arm's profit fell because the company is deliberately spending more to build its online shopping business - management says this is a planned phase, not distress. The newer, more complicated story is that Jio just became its own separately listed company via an IPO, so going forward you can watch Jio's numbers on their own, but RIL's reported profit will now also show a small slice carved out for Jio's new outside shareholders.
analysis.quarters: Total income for the September 2026 quarter rose roughly 28% year-on-year, with O2C segment EBITDA up 67.9% YoY - likely margin-led given a cyclical refining-margin recovery rather than new capacity. Jio's profit after tax rose 13.7% YoY, with management noting 5G/UBR network capex is largely complete and capex intensity should taper from here. Reliance Retail's profit fell 24.3% YoY, which management attributed to planned digital-commerce investment, absorbed input-cost inflation, and the festive season shifting entirely into Q3 - a timing and investment effect, not a demand collapse. Note: independent sources report meaningfully different consolidated net profit figures for the same quarter (roughly ₹25,548 crore to ₹29,550 crore, growth variously cited as 27%-41% YoY) - this likely reflects how much of Jio Platforms' newly listed minority interest each source is netting out post-IPO. Treat any single headline profit number with caution until checked against the company's own filed P&L.
analysis.performance_read: The uncomfortable fact first: despite being India's largest listed company, RELIANCE has lagged badly over the medium and long term - up only 13.44% over 3 years and 14.77% over 5 years, versus the Nifty's 21.89% and 31.04%, and versus peer ONGC's 43.98% and 107.41% over the same periods. The stock is also 18% below its January 2026 peak of ₹1,584.97. None of this is a corporate-action artifact: RIL's only recent corporate action is a 2-for-1 stock split in October 2024 (plus earlier splits in 1997, 2009 and 2017), which simply gives shareholders more shares at a proportionally lower price and is value-neutral - it is not a demerger or spin-off, so there is no distributed value missing from the price series. The underperformance versus both the index and the oil & gas peer group appears to be a genuine growth/valuation story, not a statistical illusion.
analysis.valuation_read: RIL trades around 21-22x trailing earnings, reportedly over a 100% premium to its oil & gas peer median (~9.89x). Separate why it is cheap/expensive from whether it is: the premium exists because the market values RIL as a Jio-plus-Retail growth story layered on top of a commodity refining business, not as a pure oil & gas major - hence the gap to an E&P peer like ONGC. Whether that premium is justified is an open question: reported ROE and ROCE are only in the high single digits (estimates range 6.7%-9.1% across sources), which is low for a 21x multiple, meaning the valuation is effectively a bet on future Jio and Retail monetisation (which management itself frames as an FY28-29 event) rather than a reflection of current returns on capital.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter is real but mixed in character. The O2C jump looks margin-led - a cyclical refining-margin recovery rather than new volume, which per se is less durable in a commodity business. Jio's growth is a steadier mix of subscriber/tariff gains (volume plus pricing). Retail's near-term numbers show a deliberate margin dip as the company funds digital-commerce investment from store cash flows - management explicitly frames FY27 as a scale-building phase and FY28-29 as the phase where that scale is meant to convert into profit, so current retail growth is not yet margin-accretive.
analysis.health_read: Leverage looks manageable: debt-to-equity is reported around 0.41x with net debt near ₹1.23 lakh crore, which is moderate against the group's scale. The bigger question is business risk, not financial risk - capex remains heavy (₹40,010 crore in this single quarter) spread across O2C expansion, Jio's network, retail footprint, and New Energy giga-factories, meaning free cash flow is being absorbed by growth investment across three large segments simultaneously rather than flowing through cleanly to shareholders.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold approximately 50.4-50.5% with zero pledge reported, which removes any promoter-leverage overhang. Institutional ownership is broad-based rather than concentrated: FIIs around 17.2%, DIIs around 21.1%, public about 11%, and a small government stake. No single marquee outside investor stands out in the data gathered here - ownership looks like standard broad-based mutual fund/insurer/FPI participation rather than a concentrated high-profile holder. Not verified - check Screener's shareholding page for exact named institutional holders.
strengths: O2C segment EBITDA rose 67.9% YoY in the September 2026 quarter, pointing to a genuine refining-margin recovery.
Jio Platforms' PAT grew 13.7% YoY with management flagging that 5G/UBR network capex is largely complete, which should ease future capital intensity.
Zero pledge against the promoter group's roughly 50.5% holding removes a common governance risk seen at other large Indian conglomerates.
Debt-to-equity of about 0.41x with net debt near ₹1.23 lakh crore keeps leverage at a manageable level despite heavy ongoing capex.
watchpoints: 5-year return of just 14.77% trails the Nifty's 31.04% and peer ONGC's 107.41% by a wide margin - a serious long-term underperformance for India's largest listed company.
Reliance Retail's PAT fell 24.3% YoY on planned digital-commerce investment; management's own FY28-29 payoff framing means this needs to show results, not just continue as a cost.

Reported consolidated net profit for the same quarter varies by roughly ₹4,000 crore across sources (₹25,548 crore to ~₹29,550 crore) - likely tied to new minority-interest accounting after the Jio Platforms IPO - so headline profit figures should be checked against the company's own filed numbers.

ROE and ROCE in the high single digits (estimates 6.7%-9.1% depending on source) sit well below what a ~21x earnings multiple typically implies, meaning the stock is pricing in future monetisation, not current capital efficiency.
analysis.one_thing: Jio Platforms now reports as a separately listed company - its standalone subscriber, ARPU and margin trajectory over the next few quarters is the clearest test of whether management's 'build scale in FY27, monetise in FY28-29' roadmap is on track, and that will be the main driver of whether RIL's own valuation gap versus the Nifty closes or widens.
